definitions.explanation: Strikingly unusual or odd, enough to attract attention or cause discomfort.

examples.japanese: {奇異|きい}な{目|め}で{見|み}られた。
{周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}が{奇異|きい}の{目|め}で{見|み}ているのに{気|き}づかないようだった。
examples.english: He didn't seem to notice the people around him looking at him strangely.

notes:
A somewhat formal word for strangeness that implies something is unusual enough to draw attention. Often used to describe how others perceive unusual behavior.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {奇異|きい}な{目|め}で{見|み}る — to look at someone strangely
- {奇異|きい}の{目|め} — strange looks, looks of bewilderment
- {奇異|きい}に{感|かん}じる — to find something strange
- {奇異|きい}な{光景|こうけい} — a bizarre sight
- {奇異|きい}に{映|うつ}る — to appear strange

USAGE:
The phrase {奇異|きい}の{目|め}で{見|み}る / {奇異|きい}な{目|め}で{見|み}る is the most common usage — it means to stare at someone as if they are bizarre. This expression implies social judgment and discomfort.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {奇妙|きみょう} — strange, curious (lighter, can be intriguing)
- {不思議|ふしぎ} — mysterious, puzzling (more neutral, can be positive)
- {異様|いよう} — bizarre, abnormal (stronger, more alarming)
